facts.title: Ancient Mexican Cultures Counted in Base 20
facts.summary: Mesoamerican cultures in what is now Mexico counted in base 20, using a vigesimal number system that spread from Mexican cultures to the rest of Mesoamerica.

facts.title: Axolotls Never Really Grow Up
facts.summary: Axolotls become adults without growing up in the usual amphibian way.

facts.title: Chocolate, Vanilla and Avocado Are Native to Mexico
facts.summary: Chocolate, vanilla and avocado are all native Mexican ingredients, along with guava, squash and a great variety of chili peppers.

facts.title: Maize, Tomatoes and Beans Were First Domesticated in Mexico
facts.summary: Mexico is where maize, tomatoes and beans were first domesticated, and the surplus these crops produced helped people settle into farming villages.

facts.title: Mexico City Is Sinking
facts.summary: Mexico City is sinking because it pumps too much water from the ground beneath it.

facts.title: Mexico City Is the Oldest Capital in the Americas
facts.summary: Mexico City is the oldest capital city in the Americas and one of only two founded by Indigenous peoples.

facts.title: Mexico City Was Built on a Lake
facts.summary: Mexico City stands on the bed of a lake.

facts.title: Mexico City's Marble Palace of Fine Arts Is Sinking Into the Ground
facts.summary: Mexico City's Palacio de Bellas Artes is so heavy that it has been sinking into the city's soft ground since work on it began.

facts.title: Mexico Has More World Heritage Sites Than Any Other Country in the Americas
facts.summary: Mexico has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country in the Americas and ranks seventh in the world.

facts.title: Mexico Is a Federation of 31 States Plus Mexico City
facts.summary: Mexico is a federal republic of 31 states plus Mexico City, which together make up its 32 federal entities.

facts.title: Mexico Is One of 17 Megadiverse Countries
facts.summary: Mexico is one of the world's 17 megadiverse countries and is home to about 10 to 12 percent of the planet's biodiversity.

facts.title: Mexico Recognises 68 Indigenous Language Groups
facts.summary: Mexico's federal government recognizes 68 Indigenous linguistic groups, made up of 364 language varieties, alongside Spanish.

facts.title: Teotihuacan Was One of the World's Largest Cities
facts.summary: At its height, roughly in the first half of the first millennium AD, Teotihuacan, about 40 kilometres northeast of today's Mexico City, was the largest city in the Americas and possibly the sixth-largest in the world.

facts.title: Wild Axolotls Survive Only in One Mexican Lake
facts.summary: Wild axolotls now survive only in Lake Xochimilco, on the southern side of Mexico City, and the species is assessed as Critically Endangered.
